fullPassage: Compared to other animals, human beings have an unusually long pre-adult existence, and it would be absurd to claim that this is simply to extend a period of suffering. Instead, much of the evidence suggests that evolution has given us our teenage years for a very good reason — in the long run they help us to succeed as individuals. It is a time when we can play a little, live a little, and grow up a little. Sometimes we are given the impression that adolescence is a time filled with extreme danger and stress. Obviously, nothing comes without risk, but we should never lose sight of the fact that being a teenager is a unique opportunity to experiment with the world, ourselves, and other people. Things may seem very serious at the time, but few of our teenage actions have long-term consequences for when we are older. I sometimes worry that we make teenagers too frightened to try new things — after all, life is for living. Everyone should have been just a little bit irresponsible before they get to twenty.
